text.p: Addressing the fact that everything a child touches falls on the floor and then is put directly in the mouth, Playskool is introducing a line of products and toys made with a new antibacterial material.
The division of Hasbro Inc. will have in full distribution by the late Spring a line of juvenile items using Microban antibacterial production.
After what it called a highly successful test marketing and national rollout of the 1-2-3 High Chair last year, which had Microban in the slide-out food tray, Playskool decided to add to the line.

Microban, created by the Microban Products Co. of Huntersville, N.C., is an additive to plastics and other materials that is designed to eliminate the growth of a broad range of bacteria, mould, mildew and fungi. It is odourless, colourless and tasteless and products containing Microban are registered with the Environmental Protection Agency, the Food and Drug Administration or the Department of Agriculture, depending on the specific use.

New Playskool toys containing Microban include the Colour Surprise Hourglass ($10.99, ages six months and up); Create-a-Song electronic toy ($24.99, ages 12 months and up); and Busy Beads Pal ($10.99, ages six months and up); all of which are currently available.
By the late spring, Playskool said, five more toys with Microban will be available in major children's and toy stores.
They are: My First Chime Weeble -- $7.99, ages three months and up. The Weeble hippo and panda bear wobble with just a gentle touch.
Nest n' Wobble Weebles -- $12.99, ages six months and up. Three wobbly Weebles in graduated sizes, which nest inside each other.
Teddy Bear -- $15.99, ages six months and up. The plush bear is a modern rendition of the toy classic.
Soft Bear -- $9.99, ages six months and up. It is made of easy to grasp fabric and contains a hidden rattle.
Frog Waterpal -- $9.99, ages 18 months and up. A green bathtime friend has an inner tube that can be taken on and off.
For more information, contact Playskool at 401-431-TOYS (8697).

In case your child doesn't spend enough time in front of the computer, a new book is designed to change all that. "Kids Rule the Net -- the only guide to the Internet written by kids" has just been published by Wolff New Media ($14.95, $C20.95).

But it's not only for kids. The book answers some very basic questions that adults might be too embarrassed to ask, such as, What is the Internet, anyway?, Is the Internet the same as the World Wide Web? and What's a Web site?
The answers are simple, straightforward and accurate.
The book then samples many of the Web sites of interest to children, and has reviews of the sites by kids who range in age from seven to 14.
Categories include animals, history, stars and heroes, science, sports, travel and, of course, aliens, UFOs and horror movies.

For parents who are afraid their children's minds will turn to mush, a lot of attention is given to books and authors. There are sites for Roald Dahl fans, Alice in Wonderland, Dr. Seuss, Madeleine L'Engle (author of "A Wrinkle in Time"), Goosebumps books and Anne Frank, whose "Diary of a Young Girl" is still among teens' most-read books.
For more information, call Wolff New Media at 212-308-8100, fax 212-308-8837 or e-mail at editors(at)ypn.com.
3M, the company that makes Scotch brand tapes and Post-it notes, will introduce a new product that "fills a consumer need for pre-cut tape strips in just the right length."
Scotch Pop-Up tape strips and dispensers come in pre-cut pads of 75 strips each, enough tape to wrap 15 average packages.
"The company came up with the idea after observing people tear off and line up pieces of tape for convenience while gift wrapping," 3M said in a statement.
The pads fit into a wearable dispenser that can be put on the fingers, knuckles or wrist. A weighted pop-up dispenser is designed for countertops and desktops.

The new pop-up tapes will be commercially available in May. Suggested retail prices are $11.99 for the weighted dispenser with two tape pads, $3.99 for the wearable dispenser with two tape pads, and $2.99 for a package of three refill pads of pop-up take strips.
